subject: Banking
title: Fedwire and Domestic Speed
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fedwire and Domestic Speed usable.

hook.text: Fedwire settles $4.7 trillion daily between US banks. Every transfer is final and irreversible within minutes.

buildup.text: Fedwire is a real-time gross settlement system. Each transfer settles individually, not in batches at end of day.

discovery.text: Finality matters. Once Fedwire confirms a transfer, the money cannot be recalled. This eliminates settlement risk.

twist.text: Fedwire only operates during business hours. A wire sent at 5pm Friday waits until Monday for processing.

climax.text: Fedwire is fast during business hours but stuck in a 9-to-5 world. Real-time means real-time only sometimes.

punchline.text: $4.7 trillion daily. Irreversible and fast, but only on weekdays.

quiz.question: What makes Fedwire different from batch settlement systems?
options: Each transfer settles individually in real time with immediate finality

details.summary: Fedwire is the Federal Reserve's real-time gross settlement system that processes high-value domestic payments between US banks, settling each transaction individually and irrevocably within minutes.
details.whyItMatters: Fedwire is the backbone of the US financial system, transferring over 4 trillion dollars daily. Its real-time finality makes it essential for time-critical transactions like real estate closings and securities settlements.
takeaways: Fedwire settles each payment individually in real time
It processes over 4 trillion dollars in transactions daily
Settlement is final and irrevocable once completed

faq.question: Who can use Fedwire?
faq.answer: Only banks and certain financial institutions with Federal Reserve accounts can access Fedwire directly. Individuals and businesses initiate wire transfers through their banks, which then use Fedwire to move the funds.

faq.question: Why are wire transfers so expensive if they are just electronic messages?
faq.answer: Banks charge $15 to $45 per wire to cover operational costs, compliance checks, and the guaranteed finality of settlement. The fee also reflects the service's immediacy compared to slower, cheaper alternatives like ACH.
